title: Browser-use provider registration and Session ownership
summary: The browser-use service only registers one provider name per composition; each provider brings its own tools through the normal tool pipeline, and browser resources belong to the exact agent and session that opened them.
firstReason: Not forcing a common browser action interface before a second real consumer exists is sound, and providers that speak MCP fit the plugin-process model directly.

title: Computer-use provider registration
summary: The computer-use service only registers one provider name per composition and defines no shared action interface; each provider exposes its own tool catalogue.
firstReason: The reasoning is the same as for browser use: one active provider, and no premature common interface.

title: Independent LibreOffice kit ownership
summary: The LibreOffice conversion engine lives in its own repository with its own releases; the harness consumes an exact published version and owns only the adapter, authorization, conversion lifetime and UI.
firstReason: Keeping the engine outside the harness build is right, but it cannot be consumed as an npm package with a Node worker; the Go host must drive a conversion engine as a separate process.

title: Bounded shared Office conversion
summary: Office-to-PDF conversion goes through one shared queue with bounded readers, queue length and source bytes and a result cache keyed by content digest; cancelling one consumer does not cancel a conversion that another consumer shares.
firstReason: Bounded, shared conversion is a resource-safety rule that does not depend on the engine; keep it.

title: On-demand Office tools for rendering, conversion, and recalculation
summary: Office rendering, conversion and recalculation are three host tools (`office_render`, `office_convert`, `office_recalculate`) that appear only in sessions that load an Office skill. They call the Office kit service inside the host, so they share the queue, limits and cache of Office previews instead of running a LibreOffice command line through the sandboxed shell.
firstReason: Host tools behind one queued service give the same result in every deployment, which a shell command under a sandbox did not. The tool contract carries over unchanged; the Go host cannot load the Node LibreOffice Kit module in-process, so the document area must choose how the engine is hosted (a supervised helper process is the likely form).

title: Defer Office background scheduling until a consumer needs it
summary: Proposal: remove foreground and background priorities from the Office document conversion queue, because nothing in the product ever submits a background request; keep the queue's general resource limits.
firstReason: Adopt: the Go conversion queue should be built with resource limits only, and gain priorities when a real background consumer exists. Building the unused scheduling machinery again would repeat the debt the note identifies.
